doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Nat Adderley as mentor and fixing his embouchure
summary: Nat told his mother to have a lawyer check any contract; after Bell's palsy hurt his playing, Parsons gave him lip exercises that restored it, and Nat sat in on his Orlando gig.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: “And make sure,” he said, “A lawyer can make sure it’s legally binding but I know what it means in the business.” And he kept at it. And it was like that. And he told Nat Junior © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

and Alison, his two kids, he said, “Look, y’all have a brother, his name is Longineu, that’s my son too.” Well Nat had Bell’s Palsy. And so he lost the one side of his face, the feeling. So anyway it gradually got better, but he couldn’t play. He had me playing some stuff in his place, some of the gigs and stuff. And then, but when he could try to play the horn again it really wasn’t good, he had really lost it. And so I told him, “Nat,” you know, “there are things we can do to help you with that.” “Well no, the doctor told me that’s the best it’s going to get.” So I’m like I don’t care what the doctor said, I can help you. So he argued me down you know, because he was obstinate boy, Nat, you know, he was going to be right. So anyway I had a gig in St. Augustine and he was living in Lakeland so I called him up I said, “Nat, after my gig tonight, I’ll get off about” whatever “I get off at 1 A.M. I’m going to drive to Lakeland and then I’m going to give you these exercises that are going to straighten your lips out. And if it doesn’t work for you I’ll pay you for the lesson.” So he couldn’t say anything. He said, “All right, come on, come on.” So I went and we had breakfast and I gave him the exercises and I demonstrated how to use them and stuff like that. And then he gave me the highest compliment, he says, “Do you know what you are Longineu? Do you know what you are?” Oh goodness, what’s this. “Do you know what you are?” “No, Nat, what is that?” “You’re a motherfucker.”

Yeah. So anyway so his wife Ann said, “Okay Longineu I’m going to make him do it, I’m going to make him do it.” So a couple of months later I’m on a gig in Orlando, in comes Nat Adderley holding his horn case. Now all before Nat had been telling me, you know, you don’t come and sit in on my gigs ‘cause you ain’t going to make no reputation on me [mumbles]. All out of love, you know, fun. So here he is coming up to me, “Hey man, can I sit in?” “What?” “Yeah.” “What is this?” So he came and pulled out his horn and he sounded like the old Nat Adderley. He wanted to show me that this did this for him.
Aw, bless your heart. I didn’t know any of that.
